---
title: "Getting started"
---

## Install

Add the package directly from GitHub:

Run:

`uv add "tiny-dsa @ git+https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-tiny-dsa"`

The package import path for the calculation functions is `tiny_dsa.api`.

## A first projection

The API takes the country profile values and the scenario inputs explicitly.
The default profile contains three countries, in this order:
`Borvelia`, `Litellia`, and `Aurelium`. The three debt values must stay aligned
with that order.

```{python}
from tiny_dsa import api, data
from tiny_dsa.runtime import as_records

baseline = api.compute_output_baseline(
    api.OutputBaselineInputs.from_defaults()
)

as_records(api.compute_output_baseline, baseline)
```

The result is a labelled series for projection years 1 through 5. With the canonical
defaults, the values are approximately 61.29, 62.09, 62.39, 62.19, and 61.49
percent of GDP.

## Add a shock

Choose one shock type:

| `shock_type` | Parameter affected | Default magnitude |
|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | Real GDP growth | -2.0 percentage points |
| 2 | Real interest rate | +2.0 percentage points |
| 3 | Primary balance | -1.0 percentage points |

`shock_year` is the first affected projection year. The selected magnitude is
then applied in every subsequent year.

```{python}
scenario = dict(
    country_name="Borvelia",
    country_initial_debt=data.COUNTRY_INITIAL_DEBT_DEFAULT,
    growth_baseline=data.GROWTH_BASELINE_DEFAULT,
    interest_baseline=data.INTEREST_BASELINE_DEFAULT,
    primary_balance_baseline=data.PRIMARY_BALANCE_BASELINE_DEFAULT,
    shock_year=2,
    shock_type=1,
    shock_magnitudes=data.SHOCK_MAGNITUDES_DEFAULT,
)

shocked = api.compute_output_shocked(
    api.OutputShockedInputs.from_defaults(**scenario)
)
delta = api.compute_output_delta(
    api.OutputDeltaInputs.from_defaults(**scenario)
)
as_records(api.compute_output_delta, delta)
```

The first delta is zero because the shock starts in year 2. For a growth shock
with the defaults, the year-5 delta is approximately 5.09 percentage points.

## Work with labelled observations

The calculation functions return labelled series. Use `as_records` when a tidy
list of year/value records is more convenient.

```{python}
as_records(api.compute_output_shocked, shocked)
```

Each record has a `TIME_PERIOD` from 1 to 5 and an `OBS_VALUE`. A single value
can also be selected by coordinate, for example `delta.sel(TIME_PERIOD=5)`.
